name: Xbox 360 Controller
notes: XInput/Xbox360. PID is 0x02FF (Xbox One wired family), DELIBERATELY != the real Xbox360 wired 0x028E. VID stays 0x045E so it works as XInput (the companion's rumble/state gates check VendorId only, never PID) and ControllerKind::detect maps any 045E to XInput; both devnodes bind via their generic fallback hardware ids (root\HIDMaestro, root\HIDMaestroXUSB) regardless of PID. The 0x02FF PID's PURPOSE is read-side identification. Deploying this profile creates TWO devnodes, each surfacing to gilrs's WGI backend as a RawGameController: (1) the SWD XUSB companion, which WGI stamps 045E:028E (the WORKING XInput slot that drives Steam), and (2) this main IG_00 HID node, which WGI shows with its raw USB PID 0x02FF and FriendlyName 'HIDMaestro XInput Companion'. FlexInput's gilrs read side identifies OUR virtual by exactly that signature -- VID/PID 045E:02FF OR a name containing 'hidmaestro' (see gilrs_backend::is_hidmaestro_virtual_xinput) -- and tags it own-virtual, while a physical Xbox (045E:028E 'Xbox 360 Controller[ for Windows]') is kept as physical. This is deterministic and order-independent: no XInput-slot detection or state correlation is needed (an earlier design that tried to drop 0x02FF and match our pad among the 028E slots by user-index was the inverted, wrong model and is gone). INPUT goes through the XUSB companion via the SHM GipData[14] region encoded by encode::gip_from_state -- NOT this HID descriptor. This descriptor exists so the sibling HID node enumerates with a sane gamepad identity (DirectInput) and to supply inputReportSize. Sticks X/Y left + Z/Rz right (int16); triggers Rx/Ry (uint8); hat + 8 buttons.
